the power output fluctuations of a future PV fleet in the Negev can be minimized by distributing PV power over a sufficient number of sites.

the assessment of power fluctuations of future PV fleet.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for the case of the Negev desert the optimal PV fleet distribution is the one with the minimum rank.

the best way to minimize the power fluctuations of a PV fleet is to install PV plants on as many sites as possible, each with a low installed power, while keeping the total installed PV power at a given level.
for a given PV fleet size the best geographical distribution for the fleet is the one which minimizes the number of extreme irradiation fluctuations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for a given total PV capacity, the PV fleet configuration that will have the minimum number of power fluctuations is the one with an equal PV power distributed between all the possible sites in the Negev desert.
a large scale deployment of PV fleet in an isolated system can be done with minimum impact on system frequency by selecting a proper spatial distribution.
the PV power plants in the Negev should be distributed over a large area with a low power capacity on each site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to distribute PV power in a way that reduces the number of extreme fluctuations.
it is better to distribute a fixed PV power over more sites than to concentrate it in fewer locations.
it is possible to select a proper spatial distribution for a PV fleet in the Negev desert that limits the power fluctuations and thus reduces the risk for the power grid stability.
